title: Research and metrics: replace confident guesses with evidence
outcome: Plan a small usability study and interpret product metrics without confusing clicks with success.
useCase: Design reviews, feature experiments, and analytics interpretation.
benefits: Makes UX decisions explainable and revisable.
drawbacks: Small studies and incomplete telemetry have limits.
version: Web UX · WCAG 2.2 · principles, not magic formulas
cue: Observe the task. Define the denominator. Keep a guardrail.

trace.title: Question
trace.detail: Start with a question: can an agent find and assign the oldest urgent ticket? Give a realistic task without teaching the intended path. Observe hesitation, wrong turns, recovery, and completion. Ask neutral questions; “Was the new button easy?” biases the answer.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Hypothesis → task or event definition → collect evidence → distinguish observation from interpretation → choose a repair → test again. Keep quotes and observed behavior separate from your explanation of the cause.

For a funnel, ask who is excluded, whether events can duplicate, and whether missing telemetry correlates with failure. A rising completion rate can reflect a changed denominator rather than a better interface.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Leading tasks teach the answer. Vanity metrics reward activity without outcome. Changing several things at once makes attribution difficult. Analytics may miss the people who could not even start.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Plan a small usability study and interpret product metrics without confusing clicks with success. Explain one example and one failure.
